title: Simple Financial Management in Housewife Communities: A Qualitative Study on Daily Financial Management Patterns
authors: Efendi, M. I.; Widagdo, C. S.
venue: International Journal of Applied Economics, Accounting and Management (IJAEAM)
tldr: Housewives in Salatiga, Indonesia develop sophisticated financial management through nuanced recording systems, community-based risk management, and social financial networks.
problem_and_motivation: Conventional understandings portray housewives in resource-constrained environments as financially vulnerable, but limited research explores their adaptive strategies and sophisticated practices.
approach: Qualitative case study using in-depth interviews, non-participant observation, and document analysis with 25 housewives in Salatiga, Indonesia.
Data analyzed through open, axial, and selective coding to integrate findings around core themes.
Findings validated through member checking, peer debriefing, and triangulation.
findings: Housewives develop nuanced recording systems for tracking daily financial transactions.
Community-based risk management through informal financial mechanisms provides resilience.
Social financial networks serve as both safety nets and investment vehicles.
Partial communication patterns where financial discussions limited to big decisions only.

definitions.definition: Indonesian rotating savings and credit association.

topics.name: Culturally Specific Financial Practices
topics.justification: Documents culturally specific Indonesian household financial management practices.

topics.name: Expense Categorization Frameworks
topics.justification: Describes nuanced recording systems for categorizing daily expenses.

topics.name: Budgeting Strategies as Domain Knowledge
topics.justification: Detailed findings on household budgeting strategies in resource-constrained settings.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides rich qualitative evidence of sophisticated financial management among housewives in a developing economy. Challenges deficit-based narratives by demonstrating agency and strategic economic navigation within bounded structures.
directly_justifies: Housewives develop complex adaptive financial strategies despite economic constraints.
Social financial networks serve as critical infrastructure for household financial resilience.
limits: Indonesian context limits direct applicability to Filipino populations.
Qualitative design with 25 participants limits generalizability.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains. Flagged 2.A, 7.A (high), 3.A (medium). Rejected 1.A-1.C as Indonesian not Filipino context; algorithmic topics (4.B-14.C) as this is qualitative.

limitations: Single-city study in Salatiga, Indonesia limits geographic generalizability.
Small sample (25) for a qualitative study limits transferability.
remember_this: Housewives develop sophisticated informal financial management systems.
Community-based risk management compensates for lack of formal financial access.
Social financial networks are critical for household resilience.
